description: MikroTik CRS354-48G-4S+2Q+RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch. It has 48 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports, four SFP+ cages, two 40G QSFP+ cages, a 10/100 management port and an RJ45 serial console, and runs RouterOS. The front carries the 48 jacks in four blocks of six columns by two rows. They are numbered 1 to 48 as printed, with the odd number on the lower jack of a column. The four SFP+ cages are numbered 1 to 4 and the two QSFP+ cages 1 and 2, each pair stacked, with the odd number below. The right-hand end carries the CONSOLE and MGMT jacks, the RESET button and the PWR 1, FAULT and PWR 2 lamps. The rear carries two AC inlets (POWER 1 and POWER 2, 100-240 V), three fans and two vent fields. The power supplies and the fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays.

ac-input-rating.note: Each inlet prints "100-240 V ~1.5A MAX, 50/60Hz" under POWER 1 or POWER 2 (photograph 1900); the brochure's range is 100 - 240 V and the quick guide's "2xAC input (100-240 V AC)".

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The product page lists two AC inputs, two PSU slots and "3 fans"; the brochure lists "Redundant supply: Yes" and two IEC cords in the box. The rear photograph shows a plain panel with the two inlets on it and no removable module, and no held document prints a supply module part number, so the supplies are built in: part of the chassis, not bays. The three round openings of the rear carry a fan behind each (the page counts three fans), so they are fans of the chassis, drawn as fan openings; the hex fields between the inlets are vents.

chassis.note: 443 wide, 44.3 high, 297 deep, from the drawing (443, 44.3 and 297 on its front, side and top views). The brochure and the product page print "297 x 443 x 44 mm", depth first and the height rounded; the same box, and the drawing's figures are carried. The 7 mm the top plan dimensions is the pair of power-cord retaining loops standing off the rear (cable management brackets in the box), not part of the depth. 443 is the body between the ear folds.

colour.note: The pilot's face (#dadada) and plate (#bebebe) are carried: the photographs are rendered studio views whose face reads #bab8b5, darkened by the lighting.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code, QCA9531 CPU at 650 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 32 MB flash, one 100 Mbps and 48 1 GbE ports, four SFP+ and two QSFP+ cages, RouterOS licence level 5, AC supply 100 - 240 V, redundant supply "Yes", serial port RJ45, 297 x 443 x 44 mm, -20 to +60 C, 60 W maximum. The product page adds the switch chip 98DX3257, two AC inputs, two PSU slots, three fans, 50 W without attachments. The 60 W is the brochure's and the page's "Max power consumption", unqualified, and is filed as the maximum; the page's 50 W is the figure without attachments.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure and product page, Included: Rackmount ears, K-48 screw kit). The drawing's side view shows the ear plate at the front end of the body, on the face, so the shipped position is flush; the top plan shows no ears (443 is the body). The ears are not drawn. The cable management brackets in the box are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Four jack blocks of six columns by two rows on the 13.97 mm pitch, the first jack housing at 9.9 mm and the blocks 88.4 mm apart, so the gutter is 4.58 mm. The SFP+ block is 30.3 mm wide at 362.3 mm, two columns of 15.3 mm, two cages high with the lamp strip between; the QSFP+ block 20.9 mm wide at 396.1 mm; the console and management jacks a 18.3 mm block at 418.6 mm. The block frames run from 12.2 to 38.7 mm. The jack row pitch is the pilot's 13.4 mm, which the drawing's outlines (13.2 to 13.7) agree with. Colours are the pilot's (face #dadada, plates #bebebe): the studio render's face reads #bab8b5, darkened by its lighting.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body measures 1164.7 px across at 200 dpi for the printed 443 (2.629 px per mm) and 115.2 px down for the printed 44.3 (2.60 px per mm), 1 percent apart, so it is orthographic and every x and y below is taken at 2.62 px per mm from the body's top-left corner. The jack pitch then reads 13.9 mm, the registry's ganged RJ-45 pitch of 13.97, on a quantity the scale never saw.

lamps.note: The jacks carry their own two lamps in their keyway-side corners (photograph 1901). Each SFP+ column's lamp strip carries four triangles in the drawing, two to each cage; they are drawn as eight arrow lamps at the drawing's positions, the QSFP+ strip as the two arrows at its ends with four slots between them (decor). The PWR 1, FAULT and PWR 2 lamps sit in the strip under the RESET button at 2.9, 7.9 and 13.0 mm from its left end (photograph). No document held says what a lamp shows (the brochure and the saved quick guide give no LED table), so none carries states beyond the component's own.

port-numbering.note: Printed numbers in photograph 1901: 2 4 ... 48 above the upper row and 1 3 ... 47 below the lower row of jacks; SFP+ 2 and 4 above and 1 and 3 below; 40G QSFP+ 2 above and 1 below; CONSOLE above the upper right jack and MGMT below the lower. The brochure's one 100 Mbps port is the MGMT jack, whose two lamps the photograph shows; the serial console is the CONSOLE jack.

rear-layout.note: estimated - no rear elevation is held; the positions are read off the studio rear photograph 1900. It looks down on the rear, so x is taken at 3.386 px per mm across the 443 mm body and y is estimated at 3.0 px per mm, the photograph's vertical scale for the 44.3 mm panel. They are good to about 1.5 mm in x and 3 mm in y. As seen from the rear: fans at 31.9, 70.0 and 401.0 mm (36 mm across, centred 22.3 mm down), the inlets at 116.7 and 355.0 mm, two hex vent fields at 201.2 and 260.8 mm. The legends read POWER 1 and POWER 2 with 100-240 V ~1.5A MAX, 50/60Hz under each inlet. The wire retaining loops over the inlets are accessories (the drawing dimensions only their 7 mm standoff) and are not drawn.

reset.note: RESET is a round button at the top of the right-hand end (drawing: centre 429.7, 5.0 mm, 4.2 mm across). The library's recessed reset part is used; the quick guide held gives no reset text.

side-walls.note: The drawing's side view has its rear at the left and the chamfered front corner at the right, so it is the left wall seen from the left: a vent field of 34.5 x 24.5 mm at 232.7 mm from the rear, with screws. It is drawn on the left face (x = 0 is the rear there). The isometric shows the right wall with a vent field at the same distance from the front; that one is drawn mirrored, 29.7 mm from the front, and is estimated (no view dimensions it). Heights are from the side view at 1.6 px per mm.
